newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Creditanstalt,ABN AMRO bid for Hungary's MHB bank.
newsitem.headline: Creditanstalt,ABN AMRO bid for Hungary's MHB bank.

text.p: Creditanstalt-Bankverein of Austria and the Netherland's ABN Amro Bank submitted bids for the privatisation tender of Magyar Hitel Bank (MHB), the daily Napi Gazdasag said on Friday.
Both Creditanstalt and ABN AMRO already have subsidiaries in Hungary.
The deadline for the submission of bids for the privatisation of a 89.23 percent stake in MHB, Hungary's fifth largest bank, was on Thursday.
Napi, quoting unnamed sources, said the third potential buyer, Bank Austria did not submit a bid, probably because it did not have enough information to make a decision.
APV officials were not available for comment.
APV or the government should make the decision about the sale within 60 days and the transaction is expected to be completed by the end of the year.
The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) and the International Finance Corporation (IFC), the banking arm of the World Bank have also expressed interest in buying a stake in MHB.
EBRD and IFC may buy part of the stake which the winner of the current tender will acquire.
Following the privatisation transaction the state plans to offer its remaining five percent stake to the management and employees of MHB.
